docs.title: Basic Signal Processing Tutorial 1
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will learn how to work with the commands: make_config, explore, info and quick to process your seismic waveforms.

In this tutorial we will follow this structure - Seismic files: tutorial1/data - Metadata: tutorial1/metadata - Config Files: tutorial1/configs

--tutorial
    --data
        --CA.ARBS..HH1.D.2022.32
        --CA.ARBS..HH2.D.2022.32
        --CA.ARBS..HHZ.D.2022.32
        ......
    --metadata
        --inv_all.xml
    --configs
        --typical_config.yaml
        --plotting_config.yaml

For this tutorial you need to download the seismic data here. Optionally, download the corresponding metadata.

Please, first open a terminal and type the following command to overviewall surfquake capabilities:

surfquake -h

docs.title: Generate Config Files
docs.text:
When working with seismic waveforms it might be necessary to follow a signal processing workflow and plotting configuration. Let's prepare the necessary files.

surfquake make_config -h
surfquake make_config -c typical_config -o "./tutorial1/configs"
surfquake make_config -c plotting_config -o "./tutorial1/configs"
The plotting configuration is commented to explain the functionality. The parametrization for signal processing can be found here for traces and here for streams.

docs.title: Explore your data
docs.text:
Sometimes we have really big datasets, A first view of your data coverage, including gaps. 

surfquake explore -h
surfquake explore -w './tutorial1/data/*'

In this scenario, you are using the wildcard * that means all files. No worries because only seismic traces will be readed.

Useful wildcards *Z* (all vertical components), *VALC* (only read station VALC). Wildcards are nice, but only understand file names no file headers.

docs.title: Look at the files header
docs.text:
Now let see the header of your files. This tell you a lot of infomation about what is inside the files, such as sampling rate, number of points, start time of the header...

Please review the following documentation:

surfquake info -h
surfquake info -w './tutorial1/data/*' -c 3

docs.title: Process your waveform
docs.text:
Finally it is time to play with processing. In the example we filter the traces between [0.5-8.0] Hz with a butterworth filter, zero-phase. Please review the next documentation:

Trace processing and plotting

surfquake quick -h
surfquake quick -w "./tutorial1/data/*" -c "./configs/typical_config.yaml" --plot_config "./configs/plotting_config.yaml"

Navigate and process interatively your data, see the menu on the terminal:

=======================================================
Plot Interaction Help
=======================================================
KEY             | ACTION
---             | ------
n               | Next page
b               | Previous page
w               | Add reference time
p               | Remove last reference
c               | Clear all picks
e               | Manual pick (interactive input)
1–6             | Quick picks (P/S + polarity)
d / Del         | Delete pick under cursor
v               | Open command prompt
u               | Set start time at cursor
i               | Set end time at cursor
Right-click drag | Select time window
Double left-click | Add pick
ESC / Enter     | Exit current mode
=======================================================

Sometimes, we do not want to plot the seismogram itself. It turn out to process and write the output files in our computer. This can be done adding option -a to the command. The files will be saved in H5 format with the picks, reference points and geodesic information in the header. The picks ae also save in the pick outputfolder set in the plot_config file. This file can be directly used in the command surfquake locate.

surfquake quick -w "./tutorial1/data/*" -c "./configs/typical_config.yaml" -o "./output" -a

On the other hand if you are interested in automatically save your plots, edit the following fields in your file configs/plotting_config.yaml and run another time the command with option -a:

plot_output_path: /my_output_plot_folder
show_plot: True

docs.title: Using Bash script
docs.text:
Now, how can I concatenate commands of surfquake in your terminal? The answer is creating a bash script file. Please, create a file, let's name it run_commnads.sh. Write the following commands in your file.

#!/bin/bash

# Activate your conda or virtual environment
source activate isp  # Replace with your environment manager if needed (e.g., 'conda activate surfquake')
surfquake explore -w './tutorial1/data/*'
surfquake quick -w "./tutorial1/data/*" -c "./configs/typical_config.yaml" --plot_config "./configs/plotting_config.yaml"

Ok, lets run the bash script. Open a terminal and go to the folder where you have the working directory and the run_commnads.sh file. Now write in the terminal the following commands

chmod u+x run_commnads.sh
sh run_commnads.sh

In this tutorial, we will learn how to work with the commands: quick, specplot to process your seismic waveforms.

In this tutorial we will follow this structure

  • Seismic files: tutorial/data
  • Metadata: tutorial/metadata
  • Config Files: tutorial/configs
  • Folder for the tutorial output: tutorial/time_freq, this must be created by the user.

For this tutorial you need to download the seismic data here. Optionally, download the corresponding metadata.

Please, first open a terminal, activate your enviroment and type the following command to overviewall surfquake capabilities:

surfquake -h

docs.title: Process your waveform
docs.text:
Now that you have the set up done. Let's do a spectrogram interactively and then we will save it.

Trace processing and plotting

surfquake quick -h
surfquake quick -w "./tutorial/data/*" -c "./configs/typical_config.yaml" --plot_config "./configs/plotting_config.yaml"
  • Remember in this step you can select a time window press i starttime and o endtime.

docs.title: Interactive
docs.text:
We are going to compute the spectrum, spectrogram and the Continouos Vavelet Transform.

  • Open an interactive propt pressing v. See the terminal, the directions for handle interactively the traces.
help spectrum
spectrum all loglog --mode fft

help spectrogram
spectrogram 0 5.0 50 --method fft --dates

help cwt
cwt 0 cm 6 0.5 10 -80 --dates
p

  • Now before back to picking mode, let's save for example the spectrogram.
save_tf spectrogram 5.0 50 --method fft --folder_path ./time_freq
p #back to picking mode

docs.title: Automatic
docs.text:
• In this section we are going to compute Time-Frequency objects (just as the section above), but using a config file. The advantage is that we can automate big process and save this objects for later use.

  • Please review the section related to Time-Frequency Objects to understand the output files and take advange of the its design.

  • Let's prepare the processing config file spectral_config.yaml. Below you will see that I concatenate the typical processing plus the computation of the speectrogram.

Analysis:
  process_1:
    name: 'rmean'
    method: 'linear'
  process_2:
    name: 'taper'
    method: 'cosine'
    max_percentage: 0.05
  process_3:
    name: 'filter'
    type: 'bandpass'
    fmin: 0.01
    fmax: 45.0
    corners: 4
    zerophase: True
  process_4:
      name: 'spectrogram'
      win: 5
      overlap: 75
      method: 'fft'
      output_path: absolute_path_to_your_output_folder
  • In the terminal run the quick command. The command will filter the trace, compute the spectrogram and save the time_frequency opbject on your output folder.
surfquake quick -w "./tutorial/data/*" -c "./configs/spectral_config.yaml" -a
  • Finally, we are going to open on of the files with the command specplot
surfquake specplot -h
surfquake specplot -f "./tutorial/time_freq/output_file.spec" -c "./configs/spectral_config.yaml" --plot_config "./configs/plotting_config.yaml" --split --smooth -a

I would like to tell you that, it might be possible to loop over your time-frequency objects to simply torage the image.
